match.reason: No bank point teaches circle theorems: the angle-properties card covers triangle and straight-line facts, and the radians card covers arc and segment area, so neither teaches angles in a semicircle or the same segment.

draft.title: Angles in a semicircle and the same segment
card: A diameter cuts a circle into two semicircles. An angle at the circumference that stands on the diameter is \(90^{\circ}\).
A chord cuts a circle into two segments. Angles at the circumference standing on the same arc, on the same side of the chord, are equal.

Example: \(AB\) is a diameter and \(C\) is on the circle. Angle \(ACB = 90^{\circ}\). If angle \(CAB = 35^{\circ}\), the angles of triangle \(ABC\) add to \(180^{\circ}\), so angle \(ABC = 180^{\circ} - 90^{\circ} - 35^{\circ} = 55^{\circ}\).
draft.remember: A diameter gives a right angle at the circumference. The same arc gives equal angles on the same side.

a.q: \(PQ\) is a diameter of a circle and \(R\) is a point on the circle. What is angle \(PRQ\)?
a.why: Angle \(PRQ\) stands on the diameter, so it is an angle in a semicircle and is \(90^{\circ}\). \(180^{\circ}\) is tempting because a diameter is a straight line, but the angle at \(R\) is not on that line.
a.clue: The angle stands on a diameter.

b.q: \(AB\) is a diameter. \(C\) is on the circle and angle \(ABC = 28^{\circ}\). What is angle \(BAC\)?
b.why: Angle \(ACB = 90^{\circ}\) as it is in a semicircle. So angle \(BAC = 180^{\circ} - 90^{\circ} - 28^{\circ} = 62^{\circ}\). \(152^{\circ}\) comes from forgetting the right angle.
b.clue: Find the angle at \(C\) first, then use the angles of a triangle.

wants.brief: A circle with diameter AB drawn through the centre and a point C on the circumference. Triangle ABC is drawn, with the angle at C marked with a right-angle symbol and labelled 90 degrees.
wants.why: It shows that the angle at the circumference stands on the diameter.

wants.brief: A circle with chord PQ. Two points R and S on the same side of the chord lie on the circumference. Lines from R to P and Q and from S to P and Q show angles PRQ and PSQ marked as equal.
wants.why: It shows two angles standing on the same arc in the same segment.
